chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: T. Holder strands the band; Jesse Stone takes over
summary: T. Holder absconds with the money again in Oklahoma, so the band makes Jesse Stone leader and becomes the Blue Serenaders in St. Joseph.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy
Jesse Stone and His Blue Serenaders

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Well I want to just digress a little bit.
This Booker Pittman later went to South America, didn't he?
First of all, when he left Kansas City -- see, we were all together in this Jesse Stone band from the North Dallas Club.

Now when we -- oh, that's a story that I missed. And I'm glad that you digressed. When we were in the first black nightclub in Dallas, finally it ended, with T. Holder and the Twelve Clouds of Joy. So T. Holder and the Twelve Clouds of Joy took us out on a tour. And he did the same thing that he had did with his original Twelve Clouds of Joy, he absconded with the money. He left us out stranded in this -- of all places -- back in Oklahoma.
And so therefore we had Jesse Stone with us. I told

you, now, another proficient man who was a university man from the University of Nebraska, and we made him take the band over. See? So Jesse said he didn't want the band, but we forced it upon him, and he says, 'well now the only way I can do you any good is I have to take you to my hometown,' which he was from Atchison, Kansas, but he had -- where a guy had booked him before, he had what which was called the Blue Serenaders.

So now we've transferred under that name, the Blue Serenaders, Jesse Stone and his Blue Serenaders, out of Saint Joseph, Missouri. And all this time Eddie Durham was in the band, Eddie Tompkins, my brother Keg Johnson, and we had one great hell of a band. And this drummer, John R. Davis --
